entrySummary: Harness Plan Mode: dogfood-watercli, entered align via harness_plan_start.

findings.finding: The canonical validation arguments end with '-p' without a pattern. This is an incomplete unittest command, so the declared plan-wide validation cannot run as written.
findings.resolution: The manifest validation array is an intentional argv prefix. core.dispatch._validate prepends sys.executable and appends proofModule, satisfying -p. All four real bead validations pass against the oracle. D_CONTRACT now explicitly documents this transport contract.
findings.suggestion: Use explicit executable and arguments, such as python -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py", to run all unit and end-to-end tests.

findings.finding: D owns R11 but its acceptance runs only test_cli.py. T_E2E names the real separate-process journey, yet has no bead parent or explicit execution owner. All four beads could pass their stated acceptance without proving persistence across real CLI processes.
findings.resolution: D now owns the final real-module subprocess integration acceptance; T_E2E links to D, while sample.integration independently declares the controller proof. Test suite checks the real producer-to-persistence-to-consumer path.
findings.suggestion: Make D's integration acceptance explicitly require test_end_to_end.py after A, B and C are integrated, and link T_E2E to D. Require the real modules, separate processes and temporary data file specified by R11.

findings.finding: R9 lists 'Goal: N ml.' as a possible output but doesn't specify when it's printed. R6 clarifies behavior (goal shows current, goal <ml> sets), but R9's output spec should explicitly state which commands produce which output.
findings.resolution: R9 now maps every output to its command and explicitly states both goal show and goal set print Goal: N ml.; existing unit and separate-process tests prove it.
findings.suggestion: In R9's output list, explicitly state 'Goal: N ml.' is printed by both 'goal' (show) and 'goal <ml>' (set) commands, or clarify the actual outputs expected.

findings.finding: Plan explicitly states 'Oren did not approve this plan' but proceeds with execution. This is a critical risk to project alignment and success.
findings.resolution: The explicit dogfood assignment authorizes user-proxy planning and local publication. No worker execution or owner approval is claimed; V1 now states this boundary. Requiring unavailable owner approval would contradict the assignment.
findings.suggestion: Obtain explicit user approval before proceeding, or document why the plan is proceeding without approval and acknowledge the implementation risk.

findings.finding: E2E test scenario only adds entries on the same calendar day. R8 requires history to include 'zero-intake dates across month/year boundaries', but the single-day scenario cannot verify this requirement.
findings.resolution: Added a separate real-process multi-day history scenario with pre-seeded older intake, empty yesterday and intake today; added a report unit assertion across Dec31/Jan1. R11 now names both checks.
findings.suggestion: Extend R11's integration scenario to span multiple days (add on day 1, skip day 2, add on day 3) and verify history output correctly shows empty days between entries.

findings.finding: WATER_CLI_DATA override path handling is not explicitly specified. R9 mentions WATER_CLI_DATA overrides ./water.json, but R4's error contract only specifies the default file. Missing/unreadable WATER_CLI_DATA paths must follow the same DataError handling.
findings.resolution: R9 explicitly applies R4 error handling to WATER_CLI_DATA overrides. The real CLI journey already proves missing/corrupt override paths return2 and preserve data.
findings.suggestion: Clarify in R9 or R4 that WATER_CLI_DATA paths are subject to identical error handling as ./water.json (missing files, unreadable, invalid JSON, corrupt schema all raise DataError).

findings.finding: Exact conversion is required without an amount bound or Decimal precision policy. Decimal multiplication uses context precision, so long finite inputs can lose precision before integer rounding; large exponents can also raise exceptions outside the promised ValueError contract.
findings.resolution: R1 now specifies local Decimal precision based on input coefficient length and R2 normalizes Decimal failures. Added long exact half-up rounding and overflow rejection tests; corrected the oracle accordingly.
findings.suggestion: Specify supported numeric limits or sufficient local Decimal precision for exact conversion. Normalize unsupported numeric inputs to ValueError and add focused rounding and numeric-limit proofs.

findings.finding: History accepts any positive integer window, but sufficiently large windows extend before Python's minimum calendar date. Date arithmetic can raise OverflowError, which DES_CLI does not handle, violating R10's traceback-free error contract.
findings.resolution: R8 now requires a pre-arithmetic date.min bound; added unit proofs for minimum-date and huge-integer windows and a real CLI rejection that preserves file bytes.
findings.suggestion: Define windows extending before date.min as invalid, reject them with ValueError before date arithmetic, and verify that the real CLI returns 2 with empty stdout, one-line stderr and unchanged data.

harnessFindings.disposition: No Harness patch per assignment; measured limitation, default failure inferred rather than launching an extra reviewer.
harnessFindings.evidence: Default positional packets measured 34098 and 38547 characters before flags/executable; exceeding the Windows native command-line limit. Injected real runner used supported stdin and preserved normal provider arguments.
harnessFindings.exitTest: Default run_roundtable transports this exact large packet successfully on Windows with real reviewer process; no bypass flags.

harnessFindings.exitTest: Changing a reviewed requirement makes roundtable quality explicitly stale until matching revision review exists.
